ocrText:
ATOMIC HABITS
Chapter 5: The Best Way to Start a New Habit
The two-minute rule states that when you start a new habit, it should take less than two
minutes to do. The idea is to make your habits as easy as possible to start. Anyone can
meditate for one minute, read one page, or put on their running shoes. And crucially, a
habit must be established before it can be improved.
The gateway habit — the tiny behavior that begins a larger routine — is the most
important part of any new pattern. You cannot optimize a habit that doesn't exist. The
goal is not to do one push-up, it is to become the type of person who doesn't miss
workouts.
Researchers have found that motivation is often highest before you begin a task and
drops sharply in the first few minutes. This means the most important moment is
showing up. Once you've started, it is far easier to continue. The friction of beginning is
almost always higher than the friction of continuing.
Here is a framework for implementing the two-minute rule:
« Meditate for one minute — build to ten minutes
« Read one page — build to twenty pages per session
« Put on gym clothes — build to a full workout
« Open your laptop — build to two hours of deep work
« Write one sentence — build to a complete first draft
The point is not to do the minimum forever. The point is to master the habit of showing

titleTags: Chapter 5: The Best Way to Start a New Habit
ocrText:
ATOMIC HABITS
Chapter 5: The Best Way to Start a New Habit
The two-minute rule states that when you start a new habit, it should take less than two
minutes to do. The idea is to make your habits as easy as possible to start. Anyone can
meditate for one minute, read one page, or put on their running shoes. And crucially, a
habit must be established before it can be improved.
The gateway habit — the tiny behavior that begins a larger routine — is the most
important part of any new pattern. You cannot optimize a habit that doesn't exist. The
goal is not to do one push-up, it is to become the type of person who doesn't miss
workouts.
Researchers have found that motivation is often highest before you begin a task and
drops sharply in the first few minutes. This means the most important moment is
showing up. Once you've started, it is far easier to continue. The friction of beginning is
almost always higher than the friction of continuing.
Here is a framework for implementing the two-minute rule:
« Meditate for one minute — build to ten minutes
« Read one page — build to twenty pages per session
« Put on gym clothes — build to a full workout
« Open your laptop — build to two hours of deep work
« Write one sentence — build to a complete first draft
The point is not to do the minimum forever. The point is to master the habit of showing
